To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the process of digital forensic data acquisition is a complex process that requires a formal description and that a process model is an appropriate means to achieve this.

the Advanced Data Acquisition Model is a process model for digital forensic practice that can be used as the basis for developing a generally-accepted process standard for the acquisition of digital evidence, that it is the first process model to incorporate a formal description of a process for acquiring digital evidence that is generic in nature and that is based on the ISO 17025:2005 standard for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories.
a process model for the digital forensic activity of acquiring digital evidence is needed and that such a model should be based on the Advanced Data Acquisition Model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of an advanced process model for digital forensic practice, the Advanced Data Acquisition Model, or ADAM.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

digital forensic evidence is reliable and admissible in court if: (1) the process of data acquisition is reliable, (2) the data acquisition process is documented, (3) the data acquisition is performed by a competent person and (4) the data acquisition complies with a recognised process model.
The Advanced Data Acquisition Model is a process model for the acquisition of digital evidence that has been developed to address the current lack of standards and processes for this activity.
the ADAM model provides a generic process model of digital forensic acquisition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ADAM model provides a generic process model for the acquisition of digital evidence, that it has been validated against the requirements for a forensic model, and that it has been tested against the ISO/IEC 17025:2005 standard for testing and calibration laboratories.

we are developing a model that can be used by digital forensic investigators, and others who have a role in digital forensics, to assist them in the capture of data from digital devices in a manner which is consistent with best practice and which can be used to demonstrate the reliability of the data.

we have developed a model that is a generic process model that can be used to describe any digital forensic process and that is based upon a formal model that is capable of describing the process at a level of detail appropriate to the context in which it is used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the process of data acquisition should not be viewed in isolation from other activities in the digital forensic process.
digital forensic acquisition is a complex activity that involves a number of distinct steps and sub-processes.

a process model can provide a framework that can assist in the establishment of standards and processes for digital forensic practice, and that a process model for digital forensic practice can be developed that is sufficiently generic to be used in a variety of digital forensic contexts.
